extracted.intended_audience: authors, illustrators, librarians, publishers, and readers interested in Latinx children's and young-adult literature awards
extracted.subtask_short: Pura Belpré Award eligibility and criteria
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the eligibility rules, selection principles, and purpose criteria for the Pura Belpré Award (an ALSC/ALA literary award recognizing portrayal of the Latinx cultural experience in children's and YA literature). Useful for creators and librarians checking whether a book or creator qualifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose / primary standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes a Latino or Latina author and illustrator whose work best portrays the Latino cultural experience in a work of literature for children or youth. Awarded for creating outstanding original children's (age 0–14) books that portray, affirm, and celebrate the Latinx cultural experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award specifically celebrates portrayal, affirmation, and celebration of the Latinx cultural experience; historically focused on children's books (age 0–14), with structural changes to categories beginning 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latinx identity definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "For the purpose of the award, 'Latinx' is defined as people whose heritage emanates from any of the Spanish-speaking cultures of the Western Hemisphere."

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Books considered should be outstanding original works (the page states the award is for 'creating outstanding original children's books').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page does not provide a formal definition of 'original' beyond the general criterion; originality is treated as part of the overall judgment of 'outstanding' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication location eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the award, the book must be published in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator residency/citizenship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible, the author or illustrator must be a resident or citizen of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible books must be published in Spanish, English, or both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age range / category scope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 1996 to 2020 the award recognized children's works; beginning in 2021 the author category was divided into two: one for a children's author and one for a young adult author (i.e., separate children's and YA author categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging basis (individual works)
rubrics_metrics.description: Books are judged individually, not based on the author/illustrator's body of work nor whether the author/illustrator has previously received the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection focuses on the merits of the single work submitted/considered rather than career achievements or past awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honors and non-awarding policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor books may be named, but if suitable candidates are not found, the awards will not be presented in that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee may withhold medals in years when no work meets the standards; naming honors is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-category selection allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: One person may be selected to receive the awards in both categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single creator can receive recognition in both author and illustrator categories (or both author categories after 2021) for the same or different works, per the committee's selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards structure and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: From 1996 to 2020 two medals were awarded at ALA's annual conference, one to a Latinx author and one to a Latinx illustrator. Beginning in 2021, the author category was divided into two: one for a children's author and one for a young adult author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is presented by the Association for Library Service to Children (ALSC) and the National Association to Promote Library and Information Services to Latinos and the Spanish-Speaking (REFORMA), and is given annually (it was biennial before 2009).
